title: Bundled preset and web check for a model with no input (one learnable number against the target)
description:
A model that is a single learnable number, optionally through a sigmoid, wired to a loss against the target, with no feature columns. This is the first-class model: estimate one probability (late or not) by maximum likelihood, and the mean by squared error.

Already checked (2026-11-21): core and engine support it. tinker-7ab made an unwired Bias a learned constant; engine fixtures intercept_only_mse and prob_direct_log_loss are graphs with no Input node (bias -> log_loss/target -> mean), and core/test/analyse.test.ts 'an unwired Bias pinned as the prediction of a log loss is trainable' passes. Not checked: the web app with such a graph (fit plot, equation strip, data controls, resample overlay, panels that assume an x column), the fused sigmoid path (Bias -> sigmoid Link -> log loss) with no Input, and there is no bundled preset.

So this bead is: a web-level test plus bundled presets, and fixes only where the web app misbehaves with no input column.

Files likely involved: web/src/presets/ (new presets, index.ts PRESET_SOURCES), web/test (load and train test), results/FitPlot.tsx (what it shows with no input column: probably hidden or a plain message rather than an error), CONTRACTS.md section 12 (list of bundled presets).

acceptance_criteria:
1. Bundled presets: (a) unwired Bias -> sigmoid Link -> log loss -> Mean on a binary target; (b) unwired Bias -> squared error -> Mean on a continuous target. Both load by ?preset= and train to the sample proportion / mean (test, tolerance 1e-4).
2. No panel throws or shows an error with no input column; the fit plot behaves sensibly (stated in the PR).
3. Bead notes say which web fixes, if any, were needed.
4. pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass.

title: 1-D loss curve panel: loss against one chosen parameter, others held fixed, with optional tangent
description:
A results panel that plots the training loss against one parameter while every other parameter stays at its current value. A dot marks the current value and loss and moves live while training or dragging the weight. Options:
- choose which parameter is the axis (any scalar entry: a Weight, a Bias, one entry of a Linear's W or b);
- 'explored only': paint the curve only over the range of values the student has visited by dragging or stepping, so the shape is discovered rather than given;
- show the tangent line (slope) at the current point, with its slope value.
Must work for a one-parameter model with no input column (a single Bias, optionally through a sigmoid, against the target).

Why: stage 0 and 1 of the first class. Students drag p and watch the score change, find the minimum, then see that the slope tells them which way to step (gradient descent by hand).

General mechanism, not a beginner-only special case (epic tinker-6t7). It works for any model by choosing one parameter and holding the others fixed; it is not limited to one-parameter models (compare the existing 2-D surface, which needs exactly 2 parameters).

title: First-lecture exercises and progressive disclosure
description:
Owner (2026-11-21): the same app serves the whole course, from a single-probability model in the first class to deep learning and transformers. Students have weak maths, so a lesson must be able to show very little at the start and reveal more as the course goes on. The first two classes cover maximum likelihood for a single probability, gradient descent, sigmoid, squared error, a categorical covariate, linear regression, logistic regression and softmax.

Design rule for every child: build a general mechanism, never a beginner-only special case. Disclosure is a per-preset allow-list that later lessons widen (no 'beginner mode' flag); the categorical input must extend later to embeddings and token inputs; the 1-D loss view works for any model by choosing one parameter and holding the others fixed. All lesson text comes from the preset (SPEC principle 5: the tool itself stays generic).

The children add the features, then one child authors the stage 0 to 5 exercise presets on top of them.
design: Related: SPEC.md 'Design principles' 5, the 'Lessons' row of the scope table and the later milestone 'Lessons: presets with a prompt, locked pieces and automatic checks'; CONTRACTS.md sections 10 and 12 (files and presets).

title: Probabilities without a link: log loss / cross-entropy accept any pred; out-of-range probability is a run-time error
description: Owner (2026-11-21): 'Even for probabilities, we don't need the prediction to be between 0 and 1 at the diagram stage. If the prediction is outside (0, 1) then you can throw an error at that point. I will have students try optimizing probabilities directly by hand, before going to the softmax / gradient descent version.' Today analyse.ts (~538-568) refuses a log_loss / cross_entropy whose pred is not a Sigmoid / Softmax link ('... takes probabilities, so wire a Sigmoid link straight into its pred input.'), and the engine's unfused path silently clips to [1e-7, 1-1e-7]. Typical lesson graph: unwired Bias (b = p, set by dragging its value) pinned as yhat -> log_loss with Target -> Mean -> L on a binary set; p = mean(y) minimises it.
design:
Risk: HIGH (core/analyse.ts, packages/engine, torch fixtures). Files: core/src/analyse.ts, engine/src/pieces/log_loss.ts + cross_entropy.ts, engine/src/compile.ts or engine API (probe), web state/trainSlice.ts (run stop + message), web results/LossReadout + status display, tools/torch-ref/gen.py + new fixture, CONTRACTS.md sections 4 and 7, SPEC.md line ~66 note.
- analyse: remove the 'wire a Sigmoid/Softmax link straight into its pred input' issue. Keep: log_loss needs a binary dataset, cross_entropy a classification dataset, cross_entropy pred width = numClasses, log_loss pred width 1 (shape rule). A matching link in front is still listed in fusable (unchanged fused/stable path).
- engine, unfused path: no clipping. log_loss = -(y log p + (1-y) log(1-p)); cross_entropy = -log p[class]. Rows of a cross-entropy pred are NOT required to sum to 1 (owner only asked for (0,1)); say so in CONTRACTS.
- Out of range = any value fed to an unfused log_loss / cross_entropy pred that is <= 0 or >= 1 (cross-entropy: every entry of the row, or only the picked class? -> every entry, since the student is meant to give probabilities). Detect it WITHOUT slowing or changing the jitted step: when step/evaluate gives a non-finite loss (or diverged), the web calls a new non-jitted engine method, e.g. engine.probabilityRange(model, params, batch): { node: NodeId; min: number; max: number }[] for each unfused prob loss on the loss path (borrows everything, frees everything, leak test). If any range leaves (0,1) the run stops (like divergence: parameters stay at the last finite values) and the status shows one plain sentence instead of 'diverged', e.g. 'Log loss takes probabilities between 0 and 1, but the prediction reached 1.27.' / '... reached -0.05.' / '... reached 0.' (Cross-entropy wording analogous.) Mark the loss node with the issue styling if cheap; not required.
- By hand while paused: a weight drag or typed value that puts p out of range must not crash; the loss readout (LossReadout, tinker-wha) and status show the same sentence instead of a number or 'diverged', and it clears as soon as p is back in range. Find where the web evaluates the loss after a hand edit and route it through the same check.
- Starting point: an unwired Bias inits uniform +/- 1/sqrt(d), so p may start negative; then the readout shows the sentence immediately. Acceptable (student sets p by hand); mention in PR. Do not change init.
- predict / fit plot: ŷ for a binary set may now be any real; check the fit plots (1-D and 2-D colour scale) do not crash or mis-scale badly; clamp display only if needed.
- Torch fixture: 'prob_direct_log_loss' (binary set, unwired Bias -> log_loss, Mean, a few SGD steps, with b set inside (0,1) via the fixture's params, staying in range) and optionally a cross-entropy one with Biases into a Sum? (cross-entropy needs width k: e.g. Input -> Linear(d,k) unlinked is fine if values stay in (0,1) -- only if easy). Regenerate with pnpm torch-ref, appended last so other fixtures do not move.
acceptance_criteria:
1. analyse: unwired Bias -> log_loss(pred) with Target -> Mean -> L on a binary set has no issues and is trainable; same graph with Sigmoid in front still fused. Cross-entropy with a non-softmax pred of width k has no link issue. Dataset-kind and width issues unchanged. Unit tests.
2. Engine: unfused log_loss/cross_entropy match the torch fixture(s); no clipping; probabilityRange reports min/max per unfused loss; leak test passes.
3. Training from p in range with lr too big so p overshoots 1: run stops with the sentence (not 'diverged'), params kept at last good values. Test in web state.
4. Paused hand edit of b to 1.3: readout and status show the sentence; editing back to 0.4 shows a number again. Test.
5. Minimising by SGD from p = 0.3 converges to mean(y) of the training targets (tolerance 1e-3).
6. Browser check at section 10 viewports, light/dark: the by-hand flow (drag the Bias value past 1 and back) on laptop and touch tablet.
7. pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass; CONTRACTS.md and SPEC.md updated.
close_reason: PR #80 merged. analyse no longer requires a link before log_loss/cross_entropy; unfused losses unclipped; step refuses updates when an unfused pred leaves (0,1) (stepRangeFn, StepResult.ranges); probabilityRange for paused checks; web probIssue sentence in status + LossReadout. Follow-up tinker-9tk (trainMany).

title: Pieces cannot be placed below a low y limit that does not match the visible canvas
description: Owner (2026-11-21): 'there seems to be an odd y-axis limit for placing nodes'. core/src/edit.ts positionLimits(nodeCount) caps positions at pad + (n+2)*(boxH+rowGap) vertically (and (n+2)*(boxW+layerGap) horizontally). With few pieces the y cap (~650 units for 6 pieces) lies inside the visible canvas, so a piece dropped or moved below it snaps up. Rows are ~2.5x shorter than columns, so the limit is far tighter in y.
design:
Risk: HIGH (core/edit.ts). Files: core/src/edit.ts (positionLimits and its callers addNode ~190, placeGroup/free-standing group ~627, moveNodes ~762), web/src/canvas (the callers that drop/move pieces: dnd.ts / actions.ts / Canvas.tsx), tests in core and web, CONTRACTS.md section 2 (positions) / 8 (edits).
- Rule: any spot the user can see on the canvas is a valid place. The edits that take a position (addNode, the group placement, moveNodes, and any other caller of positionLimits) accept an optional far-corner bound `limit?: [maxX, maxY]` in layout units; the effective cap per axis is max(positionLimits(count) axis, limit axis). Lower bound stays LAYOUT.pad. Without `limit` behaviour is unchanged (files, presets, tests stay deterministic).
- Web passes the visible canvas's bottom-right corner converted to layout units through the current view transform (layer view; neuron view if it places/moves pieces too), minus one box (boxW, boxH) so the whole box stays visible.
- Also check the pan clamp (viewport.ts clampView / layout.size) lets the user pan to where pieces now sit; after placing a piece low, the layout size grows so it stays reachable.
acceptance_criteria:
1. On a tall canvas (e.g. 1180x820 tablet and 1280x720 laptop, zoomed out), a palette drop or a move anywhere in the visible canvas lands where released (within the box-fits rule); unit test in core for the limit merge, web test for the drop.
2. Without limit, edit results unchanged (existing tests pass untouched).
3. Browser check at section 10 viewports, light and dark, mouse and touch.
4. pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass; CONTRACTS.md updated.
close_reason: PR #78 merged. addPiece/insertMacro/moveNodes take optional limit; canvas passes visibleLimit (visible bottom-right minus one box). Nits left: macro groups near the edge clamp per row/column (pre-existing); freeSlot nudge computed before the limit.

title: loss spikes at regular intervals late in training
description:
Owner report with screenshot: after training to a certain point, the loss curve shows sharp spikes at fixed, evenly spaced intervals (the curve is otherwise flat near its minimum; each spike decays back within a few steps). Suspected numerical issue.

First step: reproduce, recording the exact settings (dataset, n, graph, optimizer, lr, batch size, standardise, seed). Ask the owner for theirs if a repro isn't obvious. Then find which hypothesis holds; each has a quick discriminating test:
1. Adam near convergence: when gradients become tiny, the second-moment estimate v decays faster than m and the update m/(sqrt(v)+eps) briefly blows up. This gives classic periodic spikes late in training. Test: does it happen with SGD/momentum at the same lr? Does a larger eps (1e-7 or 1e-6) or a smaller lr remove it? Compare with PyTorch Adam on the same graph and data in float64 and float32 (the tools/torch-ref setup).
2. Mini-batch epoch boundary: batchSchedule keeps a partial last batch, so once per epoch a tiny batch gives a noisy, large loss and step. Test: is the spike period equal to stepsPerEpoch? Does full batch or a batch size dividing nTrain remove it? Is the spike only in the per-batch series, not trainFull?
3. float32 precision at very small loss: loss ~1e-7 relative to the parameter scale; check whether the spikes are real (also in val and trainFull) or a plotting artefact (log scale, decimation min/max, which keeps maxima).
4. Something periodic in the app: valEvery cadence, history decimation above 20k points, the frame/publish cadence (speed x frames), or the frame stalls bug (tinker-xqp). Check the spike period in steps against these.
Fix depends on the cause. Adam: maybe expose eps or clamp, documented; mini-batch: drop or merge the partial last batch (change batchSchedule; CONTRACTS s6); plot artefact: fix decimation. Add a regression test that would have caught it.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with evidence (spike period vs the hypotheses, the setting that removes it, PyTorch comparison if numerical); fix or documented behaviour agreed with the owner; regression test; screenshot of the curve after the fix.
notes:
Owner: the spikes go away with SGD. That points to hypothesis 1 (Adam, or possibly momentum, near convergence), not the mini-batch boundary or a plot artefact. Next: confirm which optimizer the owner was using; check that PyTorch Adam on the same graph, data and lr also spikes (float32 and float64). If torch spikes too, it is genuine Adam behaviour (the second-moment estimate v decays as gradients vanish, so the step m/(sqrt(v)+eps) jumps), not an engine bug. Then the owner decides: keep it (it's real), or mitigate (larger eps such as 1e-6, an AMSGrad variant, or lr decay). Any mitigation is a CONTRACTS s7 change and must keep the Adam fixture within tolerance or get a new fixture.
Owner decision: damp Adam by default. Pick the mechanism by evidence: compare a larger eps (e.g. 1e-6 or 1e-7), AMSGrad, and a mild lr decay on the spike repro and on the existing fixtures. Choose the smallest change that removes the periodic spikes without slowing normal training noticeably, make it the default Adam, and record the choice and why in CONTRACTS s7 and docs. If it changes Adam numerics, update tools/torch-ref/gen.py to the same variant and regenerate the Adam fixture (never hand-edit), keeping the 1e-4 tolerance. Note in the UI or docs only if the owner wants (no lesson text).
Owner decision (2026-11-18), after PR #44 measured the running-max-nu fix at 3-7x slower on presets: keep plain Adam; document the spikes as real Adam behaviour (torch float32 also spikes; SGD doesn't); keep only the long-run Adam fixture.

title: Arbitrary graph with prediction and loss roles
description:
Owner design (discussion 2026-11-18): the graph is an arbitrary DAG of operations; the user designates one or more nodes as predictions (ŷ) and exactly one node as the loss (L). Training minimises L; predict() returns the ŷ nodes; fit plots show a chosen ŷ. Model vs objective regions are derived from the roles (ancestors of the ŷ nodes = model; what L needs beyond that = objective) and drawn as shading behind the pieces, never as a fixed layout zone, so they can't contradict the graph and they work with free piece placement (tinker-ong).

Decisions:
- UI: role pins. A short wire stub ending in a pin labelled ŷ or L, attached to a node's output. You move a role by dragging its pin to another node's output (same gesture family as wiring). There is only one L pin, so dropping it elsewhere moves it. Coordinator recommendation, not objected to by the owner; confirm before the web bead starts.
- Every ŷ pin's width must match the dataset target (regression or binary: 1; softmax classification: numClasses), otherwise it gets an analyse issue on the pin. With several ŷ pins the fit plot header picks one (default: the first).
- The Output piece goes away. Sigmoid and softmax become ordinary link pieces, and ŷ is just the pin.
- A graph with no ŷ pin still trains if L is valid; the fit plot says 'No prediction selected.'
- The loss can be built from primitives: per-example vs single-number shapes, an explicit Mean reduction, L must be a single number that depends on at least one parameter. The weight penalty becomes graph structure (a Weights node reads a Linear's W, then norm, scale, add), drawn as a dashed parameter wire. The 5 current losses become ready-made groups that expand to primitives.
- Numerical stability: the engine pattern-matches sigmoid -> log loss and softmax -> cross-entropy into fused stable forms. The diagram stays semantic.

Big contract change: CONTRACTS s2-s4, s7-s9, s11, s12. Graph version 2 with migration from version 1 (files, presets, fixtures).

title: engine: patch jax-js 0.1.27 trace-stack leak (partialEvalFlat)
description: Found in PR #27 (tinker-klv). In @jax-js/jax 0.1.27 dist/index.js, partialEvalFlat calls newMain(PartialEvalTrace), which pushes onto the module-level traceStack, and never pops it; newMain returns an object with [Symbol.dispose]() that pops, but nothing calls it. Every traced valueAndGrad, once per compiled model, therefore keeps its Kernel/AluExp/JaxprTrace/PartialEvalTracer objects alive. About 0.32 MB per compile+2 steps, about 1.1 MB more with trainMany. The web app recompiles on every edit. Owner decision: patch locally with pnpm patch (reversible; drop it on upgrade) and draft an upstream issue for the owner to post. Fix: pop the trace frame after the traced function and graph extraction finish (try/finally or using), matching how the library uses newMain elsewhere. Check traceStack length returns to its prior value, and check jvp/vjp/grad/jit/vmap still work (full engine suite + fixtures). Owns patches/@jax-js__jax@0.1.27.patch, the pnpm patchedDependencies entry in the root package.json, an engine test, and a short section in docs/spike.md. Risk: high (patching the numeric library).
acceptance_criteria: pnpm patch applied and committed; a test shows traceStack length (or RSS) flat over 1000 compile+step+disposeModel cycles, where main grows about 0.3 MB per cycle; all engine tests and fixtures pass; draft upstream issue text (repro + one-line fix) in docs/jax-js-upstream-issue.md for the owner to post; CONTRACTS s7 notes the patch.
notes: From PR #27 review: (1) tighten dispose.test.ts's loose RSS bound (1.5 GB/1000 cycles) to a named constant around 100 MB/1000 cycles after the fix, preferably measuring heapUsed after gc() with vitest --expose-gc, and assert traceStack depth returns to baseline if it can be read. (2) Re-check the CONTRACTS s7 bullet saying random ops / np.take index arrays leave a constant buffer per compiled model that is never freed; it may be stale now that jits are disposed. (3) Pre-existing: if startTraining throws inside trainSlice resync's try, the Params from fromHost leak; dispose them in the catch.
close_reason: PR #33 merged. pnpm patch of @jax-js/jax 0.1.27 (patches/@jax-js__jax@0.1.27.patch, patchedDependencies in pnpm-workspace.yaml; dist/index.js + index.cjs): partialEvalFlat pops its trace frame (try/finally); Jaxpr.getHash hashes nested Jaxprs by content so jitCompileCache keys are stable; vmap/jvp/transpose Jaxpr caches are WeakMaps. Heap growth per 1000 compile cycles 1060 MB -> 1 MB. Reviewer: 21 single-setting variants bit-identical across shared/fresh processes (no wrong cache hits reachable). Draft upstream issue in docs/jax-js-upstream-issue.md for the owner to post; re-check the patch on any jax-js upgrade.

title: PyTorch reference fixtures: generator script and committed JSON
description:
The ground truth the engine is tested against (SPEC "Correctness"). A uv script builds each case in PyTorch on fixed inputs and writes the expected predictions, loss, gradients and optimizer trajectories as JSON in the CONTRACTS.md section 11 format.

Cases (one fixture file each; small: n = 5 to 8 rows, widths 1 to 4):
- linear with and without bias; d = 1 and d = 2.
- each activation (sigmoid, tanh, relu, gelu) between two Linears. GELU: torch default (erf form); note in the PR whether jax-js gelu is erf or tanh form if you can tell from its d.ts.
- output links: identity, sigmoid, softmax (width 2).
- each loss: squared_error, absolute_error, huber (delta 1 and 0.5), log_loss (sigmoid output, BCEWithLogits on logits), cross_entropy (softmax output, class-index targets, CrossEntropyLoss on logits), and squared_error on a sigmoid output.
- weight penalty L2 and L1 with lambda 0.1, applied to Linear weights only (explicit added term, not weight_decay; biases excluded).
- feature: degree 3 with sin, cos and products on d = 2.
- add: skip connection lin1 -> act -> lin2 plus lin1 -> add.b.
- dropout p = 0.5 with a fixed mask written to `expect.dropoutMask` (torch output computed with that mask and 1/(1-p) scaling).
- optimizers: 5 full-batch steps of sgd, sgd momentum 0.9, adam (torch defaults) on a 2-layer tanh MLP; record params after 5 steps and the 5 losses.
- a two-parameter model (1 weight, 1 bias) for the loss-surface view.

title: core/torchgen.ts: whole torch script from a graph, registry torch emitters, CONTRACTS section 14
description: Generate a whole runnable PyTorch script from a graph, in packages/core, with a span map from text ranges to node ids. Replaces the registry's torch strings with structured emitters. Writes CONTRACTS.md section 14 "Torch code" (and updates section 3's `torch` field). Read the epic (tinker-img) for the owner decisions. Pedagogical: the script must run and train sensibly; it need not match the engine numerically.
design:
Risk: high (core/registry.ts, new core module other beads depend on). Coordinator reads the diff.

Files owned: packages/core/src/torchgen.ts (+ test), packages/core/src/registry.ts (torch field only), packages/core/src/index.ts export, CONTRACTS.md section 3 (torch field) and new section 14.

API:
  type TorchSpan = { node: NodeId; from: number; to: number };   // char offsets into text; a piece may have several spans (__init__ line and forward line); a merged idiom (F.mse_loss over subtract/square/mean) gives one span per covered node over the same range
  type TorchCode = { text: string; spans: TorchSpan[]; folds: { from: number; to: number; label: string }[] };  // folds: the data literals, for the view to collapse
  function torchScript(graph: Graph, analysis: Analysis, dataset: Dataset, opts?: { steps?: number }): TorchCode | null;  // null while analysis has blocking issues; never throws

Registry: replace `torch(node, inWidth): string` with an emitter, e.g.
  torch(node, ctx: { ins: Record<string, string>  /* port -> python expr (variable name); variadic port as in, in#1, ... */; inWidth: number; shape...; self: string /* 'self.<id>' */ }): { init?: string; expr: string }
Exact shape is the implementer's choice; document it in section 3. Record<PieceType,...> stays exhaustive.

Script layout (order fixed):
1. imports: torch, torch.nn as nn, torch.nn.functional as F; sklearn.tree only when a Tree is live.
2. torch.manual_seed(train.seed).
3. Data: x_train, y_train, x_val, y_val as torch.tensor literals of the dataset's actual rows (float32; class targets as long where the loss needs it). Each literal is one fold. Standardisation (data.standardize) as explicit mean/std lines from the training rows.
4. Tree fits (if any): DecisionTreeRegressor/Classifier(criterion, max_depth, min_samples_split, min_samples_leaf, min_impurity_decrease).fit on the training rows of the Input's columns, before the model.
5. class Model(nn.Module): __init__ declares every live parameter-owning piece as self.<id>: nn.Linear(in, out, bias=...), nn.Embedding(K, width), nn.Parameter(torch.empty(1, 1).uniform_(-b, b)) for scalew / bias (bound 1/sqrt(d)). forward(self, x) runs analysis.region model pieces in analysis.order, one statement `<id> = <expr>` per piece, returns the ŷ pin(s) (tuple when several) plus any model node the objective reads (as extra return values). Parameterless pieces use the functional form (torch.tanh, torch.relu, torch.sigmoid, F.gelu, torch.softmax(dim=-1), F.dropout(h, p, self.training), F.one_hot(...).float(), torch.cat for Feature in the CONTRACTS feature column order).
6. def objective(model, x, y): calls model(x), then the objective region pieces, returns the L pin. Weights tap: model.<lin>.weight.T. Norm: .pow(2).sum() / .abs().sum(). Penalty stays an explicit added term.
7. Idioms (always on): subtract(ŷ, target)->square->mean => F.mse_loss(a, b); ->abs->mean => F.l1_loss; ->huber->mean => F.huber_loss(a, b, delta=); sigmoid link -> log_loss -> mean where analysis.fusable lists the pair => F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(z, y) on the link's input (the link still appears in forward when it is a ŷ pin; the objective uses its input); softmax -> cross_entropy -> mean => F.cross_entropy(z, y.long().squeeze(1)). Only when the intermediate nodes have no other reader. Otherwise literal (F.binary_cross_entropy(p, y, reduction='none'), etc.).
8. model = Model(); optimizer: torch.optim.SGD(lr) / SGD(lr, momentum=0.9) / Adam(lr). steps = opts.steps ?? 1000. Full batch: loop over steps on x_train. Mini-batch: TensorDataset + DataLoader(batch_size, shuffle=True), cycling. Print train and validation loss every steps/10 and at the end (model.eval() for validation).

Names: node ids are the variable names. An id that is a Python keyword or collides with a script name (x, y, self, model, torch, nn, F, np, optimizer, step, loader, x_train, y_train, x_val, y_val, objective, Model, and the like) gets a trailing `_` (repeat until free). Inert pieces are omitted. Column/Input indices are dataset column positions. Number formatting: reuse the registry's py.float.

Tests: golden text tests for (a) 1-D MLP with mse, (b) logistic with sigmoid+log loss (fused idiom), (c) softmax+cross-entropy multiclass, (d) skip connection with Add + dropout + feature, (e) weight penalty, (f) scalar pieces incl. unwired Bias, (g) lookup/onehot categorical, (h) tree, (i) no ŷ pin, (j) objective reading an unpinned model node, (k) id collisions with keywords/x/model, (l) mini-batch + Adam, (m) invalid graph -> null. Spans: every live node has >= 1 span and every span's text contains its node's variable name or the idiom call. Don't touch engine fixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
- torchScript exported from @tinker/core; CONTRACTS section 14 documents API, layout, idioms, naming; section 3 documents the new torch emitter.

- Manually ran the generated script for (a), (b), (c), (l) with uv + torch (note in PR): runs, loss falls.

title: Crossing wires show a clear over/under so each wire can be traced
description: Where two wires cross or overlap on the canvas they currently draw as plain strokes on top of each other, so at a crossing a user cannot tell which line continues where and loses track of the data flow. Each crossing should read as one wire passing over the other (a visible gap/casing in the under wire), so every wire can be followed by eye from source to destination.
design: Layer view: packages/web/src/canvas/Wire.tsx and the wire loops in canvas/LayerView.tsx; wire routes come from core/layout.ts (CONTRACTS.md section 9). Suggested approach: give each visible wire stroke a casing (a wider stroke under it in the canvas background colour, theme token, so it works light and dark), drawn per wire immediately before its line, so a later wire cuts a gap through earlier ones at every crossing. Stacking order must be deterministic and stable while editing (e.g. graph.edges order; a selected/hovered/lifted wire, and wires being dragged, draw on top). Dashed weights.of wires and error wires get the same treatment. The casing must not take presses (hit strokes and labels keep current precedence) and must not hide arrowheads, ports or wire labels. Alternative if the casing looks heavy: compute crossing points in core (pure, tested) and draw small hop arcs or gaps only there. Also check neuron view if its wires cross. Risk: normal (web styling/rendering; no engine/analyse change). Update CONTRACTS.md section 10 with the rule.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Two crossing wires in layer view: one visibly passes over the other with a gap in the under wire, light and dark. 2. Over/under order is deterministic (same graph, same drawing) and the selected wire is drawn over the others. 3. Partially overlapping (collinear) segments remain distinguishable or the overlap is avoided. 4. Wire presses, labels, arrowheads, ports and pins behave as before (existing tests pass). 5. Checked in a browser at the CONTRACTS.md section 10 viewports, light and dark, with a screenshot of a crossing.

title: Engine: Tree piece from host-computed one-hot; trainMany fits and pads per copy
description: The engine side of the Tree piece. Because a Tree's input is always an Input piece, its one-hot output is a fixed function of the batch rows: the engine computes it on the host with core.treeOneHot and passes it into the jitted functions as data. No fitted state in Params, no stop-gradient, no array constants.
design:
Files: engine/src/pieces/tree.ts (new), pieces/index.ts, compile.ts, many.ts, index.ts/types.ts as needed, engine tests incl. leak test, CONTRACTS section 7.
compile(graph, data, fits) (or an equivalent way to hand the core fits to the model): for every batch (predict, evaluate, step, exampleLosses, lossGrid, lossCurve, lossSlope, probabilityRange) the engine computes each tree's [n, leaves] one-hot on the host from the tree's Input columns of batch x and passes it as an ARGUMENT of the jitted function (never captured: tinker-daq). The tree piece's forward just returns that tensor; it consumes nothing else. Grids (fit plot) go through predict and so get the same treatment.
trainMany(model, seeds, data, steps): copies train on different resamples, so the engine fits each copy's trees itself (core.fitTree on data[i], training rows), pads every copy's one-hot to the largest leaf count with zero columns, initialises the padded weights of the downstream Linear to 0 (they get zero gradient and never affect a prediction), and strips the padding from the returned HostParams. Each ManyResult also returns that copy's fits, and the resampling overlay must predict each copy with ITS OWN tree (check web/src/results/resampleRun.ts and resampleWorker.ts: the overlay runs in a worker; extend whatever predict path it uses, e.g. a predict that takes fits). Bias and variance numbers must use per-copy trees.
Init of the downstream Linear follows the torch default with fan-in = that copy's/model's real leaf count.
Checks: a fixture-style test that one SGD and one Adam step on Input -> Tree -> Linear(1) -> squared error equals torch on the same one-hot (gen.py: sklearn one-hot fed to nn.Linear); leak test with a tree model (step, predict on grids, trainMany) flat; trainMany with copies of different leaf counts. Risk: HIGH (packages/engine): coordinator reads the diff.
acceptance_criteria: Tree models train, predict on grids and evaluate; gradients/updates match the torch fixture to 5 decimals; trainMany handles differing leaf counts and returns per-copy fits with unpadded params; resampling overlay draws each copy with its own tree and the bias/variance numbers are right (test with a depth-1 tree where they can be computed by hand); leak test flat; CONTRACTS section 7 updated; test/typecheck/lint pass.
notes: From PR #125 review: treeOneHot needs full-width standardised rows (fit feature = dataset column index). fitTree 5000x2 depth 8 absolute_error < 1s, fine per copy.

Tree one-hot computed on host (xHost) and appended as extra columns of x; callers still pass [n,d] rows in the standardised space. trainMany returns {params, diverged, fits}; padded vmapped path only when paddingIsNeutral (Tree feeds only Linear.in) or leaf counts equal, else per-copy compile. Predict a copy with compile(graph, info, r.fits); resampleRun.ts does this. 6h1.4 must refit+recompile+re-init on data or tree-setting change.

title: Tree node and greedy fit in core (fitTree, schema, registry, analysis)
description: A Tree piece: greedy CART splits on its input columns, output = one-hot of the leaf each example falls in. Fitted on the host from the training rows whenever the data or the tree's settings change; its output width is the fitted leaf count, so a downstream Linear reads its input width from it as it does from any upstream piece. See the epic tinker-6h1 for the decisions.
design:
Files: new core/src/tree.ts (fitTree, treeLeafIndex, treeOneHot, fitTrees), core/graph.ts (node type 'tree'), core/registry.ts (core entry), core/analyse.ts, core/equation.ts, tools/torch-ref/gen.py + fixtures, CONTRACTS sections 2, 3, 4, 11.
Node: {type:'tree', criterion: 'squared_error'|'absolute_error'|'gini'|'entropy', depth: int 1..8 (default 3), minSplit: int >= 2 (default 2), minLeaf: int >= 1 (default 1), minDecrease: number >= 0 (default 0)}. Port 'in' only; the tree reads the dataset's y implicitly (no target wire). 0 parameters. Family 'features'.
fitTree(x row-major, n, d, y, settings, kind/numClasses) in float64 on the training rows only (never validation): greedy CART as sklearn: candidate thresholds are midpoints between consecutive distinct sorted values (if the midpoint rounds to the right value use the left value); x <= t goes left; a node becomes a leaf at depth == settings.depth, n < minSplit, when pure, or when no split leaves >= minLeaf each side; split only when the best weighted impurity decrease (sklearn's min_impurity_decrease formula, N_t/N * (imp - N_L/N_t imp_L - N_R/N_t imp_R)) is > 0 and >= minDecrease. Impurities: squared_error variance, absolute_error mean absolute deviation from the median, gini, entropy (log2). Ties: lowest feature index, then lowest threshold. Leaves numbered left to right (depth-first, left child first). Returns {nodes, leaves}. treeLeafIndex/treeOneHot evaluate a fit on any rows (grids too) in float64 on the given float32 values.
Width: ShapeCtx (or the analyse input) gains the fitted leaf counts per tree node id; the tree's outShape is {kind:'example', width: leaves}. Without a fit for that node: an issue 'Tree has not been fitted to data yet.' (web always fits first). fitTrees(graph, analysis-or-inputs, dataset) fits every tree node from the training rows.
Analysis rules (one plain sentence each, block training): 'in' must be wired straight from an Input piece ('A Tree reads data columns directly; wire an Input into it.'); criterion must match DataInfo.kind (regression: squared/absolute error; binary/multiclass: gini/entropy, y as class index); no category column.
Equation: \mathrm{leaf}(x) (one-hot). Torch counterpart string: sklearn DecisionTreeRegressor/Classifier(criterion, max_depth, min_samples_split, min_samples_leaf, min_impurity_decrease).fit(x, y), then F.one_hot(torch.as_tensor(leaf ids)).
Fixtures: gen.py gains scikit-learn; fit sklearn trees on a few fixed sets (1-D regression with duplicate x values incl. clipped ends, 2-D regression, binary and 3-class classification; each criterion; depth/minLeaf/minSplit/minDecrease variations) and compare the partition of training rows into leaves and the set of (feature, threshold) splits. Never hand-edit fixtures. Risk: HIGH (analyse.ts, fixtures): coordinator reads the diff.
acceptance_criteria: fitTree matches the sklearn fixtures (partitions and thresholds) for all four criteria and every stopping rule; unit tests for ties, duplicate x, pure nodes, depth 1..8; Input -> Tree -> Linear(1) analyses with Linear in-width = leaf count and parameter count = leaves + 1; the analysis issues above fire with their sentences; parseGraph accepts and defaults the node; CONTRACTS sections 2, 3, 4, 11 updated; test/typecheck/lint pass. (Engine and web entries of the registry may be stubs that throw 'not implemented' if the Record types force them; say so in the PR.)

title: Bias-variance exercise with decision trees
description: Owner (2026-11-24): port the bias-variance game (~/teaching/bait509-shiny/bias-variance-game/app.py) to Tinker using a decision tree in place of polynomial features. Model: Input(x1) -> Tree (greedy splits, one-hot of leaves) -> Linear(leaves -> 1) -> squared error. Complexity dial is tree depth / min samples per leaf; train loss falls toward 0 at full depth while validation loss rises; Resample x20 shows tree variance. Polynomial/MLP routes were rejected: GD cannot reach the exact high-degree polynomial fit (conditioning, cond(X'X) ~1e33 even with standardised/orthogonal bases; ridge loses its smoothing meaning in an orthonormal basis); the tree is the owner's chosen route.
design: Decisions (owner, 2026-11-24): trees are fitted on the host (core, float64, training rows only) whenever the data or tree settings change, before analysis; Linear reads its input width from the fitted leaf count (no fixed 2^depth padding in the graph). Tree input must be an Input piece, so the tree's one-hot is a fixed function of the batch rows: the engine receives it as host-computed data (no fitted state in Params, no jit constants, no stop-gradient needed). The tree reads the dataset's y implicitly (no target wire). Single-purpose piece: no trees on learned features, no boosting.

title: Equation strip: model and loss as equations under the canvas
description: Owner (2026-11-21): 'add an equation display for the current model'. Chosen: show the model (each yhat pin) and the objective L as equations, with live trained values substituted for scalar-sized models; placed as a strip along the bottom of the graph canvas, beside the Group/Expand bar.
design:
Risk: normal (core pure function + web). Files: new core/src/equation.ts (pure, exported from core index, unit tested), new web/src/canvas/EquationStrip.tsx (+ css), Canvas.tsx mount, CONTRACTS.md (new subsection in section 10, function in section 3 or a new short section).
- core: `modelEquations(graph, analysis, data, host?) -> { lines: { lhs: string; rhs: string; kind: 'pred'|'loss'|'def' }[]; numeric?: { lhs; rhs; kind }[] }` returning TeX strings (no DOM). Walk from each yhat pin and from L over analysis order/inputs. Notation: Input x (or x_{[1,3]} for a column subset); Column x_j (use featureNames? no: ids x1 -> x_1); Linear k (k by order among Linears) W_k h + b_k (no b_k without bias); activation \tanh, \mathrm{ReLU}, \sigma, \mathrm{GELU}; link sigmoid \sigma, softmax \mathrm{softmax}; feature \phi(x); dropout \mathrm{drop}_{p}(\cdot); scalew w_k \cdot (...) using the SAME names the weight pills use (find the existing naming helper used by WeightPill/fmtWeight and reuse it); bias (...) + b_k, unwired Bias -> b_k; sum/add a + b + ..., subtract a - b; scale c\,(...); target y; square (\cdot)^2; abs |\cdot|; huber H_{\delta}(\cdot); log_loss \ell_{\log}(\hat{y}, y) or the explicit -[y\log p + (1-y)\log(1-p)] (pick one, say which); cross_entropy \mathrm{CE}; mean \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (...)_i; norm \|W_k\|_2^2 / \|W_k\|_1; weights tap W_k. A node whose value is used by more than one consumer gets its own definition line h_k = ... (kind 'def') and is referenced by name; a yhat node that feeds the loss is written \hat{y} inside L (so L reads e.g. L = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (\hat{y}_i - y_i)^2). Several yhat pins: \hat{y}_1, \hat{y}_2. Inert pieces are skipped; when a pin does not resolve, that line is omitted (no crash, no issue text).
- numeric: only when every live parameter is a scalar (scalew, bias) or the total live parameter count is <= 8: same lines with values substituted, 2 decimals (reuse fmtWeight), signs folded (x - 0.30, not x + -0.30).
- web: strip at the bottom of the layer-view canvas next to the ScalarBar (do not overlap it; share the row or stack above it), visible in both grain views, KaTeX via the existing Tex component, one line per equation, horizontal scroll inside the strip when long, never page overflow; collapses to a small toggle button (data-testid equation-toggle), open by default. Numeric line updates while training at most once per animation frame (subscribe narrowly; do not re-render the canvas). Tokens from theme.css, light and dark. data-testid model-equation, equation-line.
- No lesson text: just the equations.
acceptance_criteria:
1. core unit tests: linear regression (Input->Linear d->1->yhat, squared-error loss) gives yhat = W_1 x + b_1 and L = mean of squared residual; scalar model (Columns, Weights, Sum, Bias) gives yhat = w_1 x_1 + w_2 x_2 + b_1 and numeric line with folded signs; unwired Bias mean model gives yhat = b_1; MLP with tanh gives nested form; skip connection gets a def line; weight penalty shows + lambda ||W||; invalid/unpinned graph returns no line for the missing pin and never throws.
2. Strip visible under the canvas in layer and neuron view, toggles, numeric values move while training.
3. Browser check at section 10 viewports, light and dark, long equation scrolls inside the strip, no page overflow, does not cover the ScalarBar.
4. pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass; CONTRACTS.md updated.

title: Bias with optional input: unwired Bias is a learned constant (intercept-only model)

Owner chose (2026-11-19) to make Bias's input optional rather than add a new Constant piece: an unwired Bias outputs b broadcast to [n, 1]; wiring something in turns it back into in + b (so a lesson can start at the mean and then add w*x into the same Bias).

Risk: HIGH (packages/engine, core/analyse.ts, torch fixtures).

Files: core/registry.ts (bias entry; new optional-port flag), core/analyse.ts (missing optional port is not a dangling input), engine/src/pieces/scalar.ts (bias forward), engine/src/compile.ts (batch-x reference count), tools/torch-ref/gen.py + regenerated fixture, web drawing for Bias only if the unwired port needs to look different (it should still show its input port so it can be wired), CONTRACTS.md sections 2, 3, 4 and 7.

- Registry: add `optionalPorts?: readonly string[]` to CorePiece (like variadicPorts) with an exported helper `isOptionalPort(type, port)`; Bias lists ['in']. Only Bias uses it. Document in CONTRACTS section 3 next to variadic ports.
- Shape rule: bias with 'in' missing -> example(1); with 'in' wired -> unchanged (example passes through; scalar/param still an error). Param shapes stay { b: [1] }, init unchanged (uniform +/- 1/sqrt(d)). Parameter count 1 either way, so reconcileParams keeps b when the input is wired or unwired (same shapes and type).
- Analyse: an unwired optional port gives no issue; ancestry/regions unchanged (an unwired Bias pinned as yhat is in the model region and live; an unwired Bias nobody uses is still inert). inWidth for the unwired case is 0, like a piece with no ports, so paramShapes is computed.
- Engine: unwired Bias returns b broadcast to [n, 1] where n is the batch row count. Must not create array constants inside a jit or the differentiated walk (tinker-daq): derive from the batch x (ctx.takeX) or broadcast b to a static shape read from x.shape; update compile.ts xLeft so an unwired Bias counts as an x consumer if it takes x. predict, evaluate, step, trainMany, lossGrid must all work. Leak test must pass.

- Drop-to-swap: Bias and Weight (scalew) stay in 'scalars'; check whether the identical-ports swap rule must also compare optional flags (CONTRACTS section 3 says swaps need identical ports incl. variadic flags). Recommend: optional flags must match too, so Bias no longer swaps with Weight, unless that breaks an existing test the owner relies on -- report in the PR either way.
- Fixture: new torch fixture 'intercept_only_mse' (regression set, graph Bias(unwired) pinned as yhat, Target, squared error, mean as L; sgd a few steps) checked against PyTorch like the others; plus a core/engine test that after enough full-batch SGD steps b is within 1e-4 of mean(yTrain).

1. Graph: bias (no input) -> yhat pin; bias + target -> squared_error -> mean -> L pin. analyse gives no blocking issues, totalParams = 1, Train is enabled in the app.
2. Training it full batch converges b to mean of the training targets (test, tolerance 1e-4); evaluate equals the population variance of y at the optimum.
3. Torch fixture intercept_only_mse generated by gen.py (not by hand) and matched by the engine.
4. Wiring an Input/Column (or Weight*x) into that Bias makes it in + b with the same b (params kept, not re-initialised); unwiring goes back. Test in core (reconcileParams) and engine.

title: engine: log_loss and cross_entropy capture constants in traces (leak per compile)
description: Found in tinker-daq (PR #63): pieces/log_loss.ts (fused path np.zeros(pred.shape) for logsumexp([z,0])) and pieces/cross_entropy.ts (np.arange(k) for the one-hot) create array constants inside jitted traces; jax-js never frees captured constants, leaking ~2 and ~3 buffers per compile (fixtures loss_log_loss, loss_cross_entropy, link_softmax, prim_link_shared...). Rewrite constant-free (e.g. softplus-free stable form via z.ref.sub(z.ref) style zeros or maximum/abs formulation for log-sigmoid; one-hot via comparisons built from inputs without captured constants, or pass class indices through take_along_axis without constants) and add 200-cycle leak tests for classification graphs. Fixtures must stay unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: 200 compile/train/dispose cycles of logistic and softmax graphs stay flat; finite at logits ±1000; all fixtures unchanged (torch-ref no diff).
notes: PR #63 review measured: loss_cross_entropy and prim_cross_entropy_softmax +800 buffers / 200 cycles (~4 per compile), loss_log_loss +600 (~3). Sources cross_entropy.ts:20 np.arange(k), log_loss.ts:19 np.zeros(pred.shape). Suggested: zeros via pred.ref.sub(pred.ref); class iota from an existing array or take-along-axis.
close_reason: PR #65 merged. Constant-free log loss (logLossFromLogit: (z+|z|)/2 + log1p(exp(-|z|)) - z*y, correct 0.5-y gradient at z=0) and hand-written logSoftmax/softmax in pieces/softmax.ts (nn.logsumexp/logSoftmax/softmax and astype of masks under grad each leaked a captured constant); CE class pick via static slices + np.where. Leak tests flat for log-loss and CE graphs; fixtures unchanged; presets exact except logistic/xor (rel 1e-6).

title: engine: Input with a column subset leaks one buffer per compile
description: Found by the tinker-9io.4 implementer (PR #62): packages/engine/src/pieces/input.ts uses np.take with a captured np.array index constant when the Input has a column subset; captured array constants leak one buffer per compile (the Column piece avoided it with a static slice). Fix with static slices/concatenate (no captured constants) and add a leak test: 200 compile/dispose cycles of a graph with an Input subset stay flat.
acceptance_criteria: Leak test with an Input column subset over 200 compile/train/dispose cycles is flat; fixtures unchanged.
notes: PR #62 review confirmed: pieces/input.ts:13 leaks 3 buffers per compile (np.take captures np.array(idx) in predict/eval/step traces) — 150 over 50 cycles. No fixture covers a subset/reorder Input since engine/test/util.ts loadFixture now takes columns from the batch width; add a subset-Input fixture/test. Also check: a probe graph with an Input + a Linear read only by predictions (not by the loss) leaked 2 buffers per cycle — investigate against main (unread params in a pass?).
close_reason: PR #63 merged. Input subset/reorder uses static slices per contiguous run (+concatenate) instead of np.take with a captured index constant; stepFn differentiates only params the loss reads, zero grads as a.ref.sub(a.ref) (fixes a 2-buffer leak for prediction-only heads / tap-only Linear bias). 200-cycle leak tests flat; fixtures unchanged. Remaining log_loss/cross_entropy constants -> tinker-oob.

title: web: render math with LaTeX (KaTeX) instead of Unicode
description:
Owner request: 'can we get latex rendering instead of unicode?'

Math is currently Unicode text in: canvas piece drawings (drawings/output.tsx ŷ, loss.tsx δ and the λ penalty tag, feature.tsx x..x^d, activation.tsx σ/tanh/ReLU/GELU symbols), the Inspector, the bias²/variance readout (results/ResampleOverlay.tsx), pin labels (results/pinsModel.ts, Pins.tsx), axis/legend labels in the canvas-2D plots, and possibly preset prompts (presets/PromptLine.tsx). UI multiplication signs like 'Resample × 20' are not math and stay as text.

Approach to decide in the bead:
- Use KaTeX (small, fast, synchronous; no network, so fonts are bundled locally, which also suits the later offline/PWA bead). One shared <Tex> component plus a tex-to-string cache.
- SVG canvas pieces: KaTeX outputs HTML, so either embed it via <foreignObject> (check hit-testing, scaling with the layer/neuron view transforms, text legibility rules (legibleAt), and Safari/iPad foreignObject quirks), or pre-render KaTeX to an image/SVG per label. Measure the cost on graphs with many pieces and during Run (labels must not re-render per frame).
- Canvas-2D plots (FitPlot, LossCurves, LossSurface): canvas can't draw KaTeX directly, so put axis titles and legends in an HTML overlay positioned over the canvas, or draw cached rasterised labels.
- Preset prompts: decide whether $...$ in prompt text is rendered (prompts are data shown verbatim; if rendered, escape everything else; no HTML injection).
- Light and dark: KaTeX inherits currentColor.
Bundle size: report the added gzipped size.
acceptance_criteria: All math labels listed above render via KaTeX with no Unicode stand-ins left (grep check in the PR); fonts bundled, no network requests (verified in headless Chrome with network logging); legible at the s10 viewports in light and dark, including fit-scale canvas labels (legibleAt still hides tiny secondary labels); no per-frame re-render of math during Run (measured); hit-testing on pieces unchanged; bundle size delta reported; screenshots.
close_reason: PR #51 merged (owner accepted ~+77 kB gzip JS). web/src/tex/Tex.tsx: Tex, TexText ($...$ in text, rest escaped), SvgTex (foreignObject, pointer-events none), cached renderToString with trust:false, throwOnError:false. NodeShell glyph/tag take TeX (no dollars). Plot axis titles via HTML overlay plot/AxisLabels.tsx. Fonts: woff2 only via Vite plugin (dist -876 KB). CONTRACTS s10 'Math labels'.

title: web: unexplained 600-700 ms frame stalls during Run at high speed
description: Found in PR #19 review and follow-up: at speed 50 the training loop shows 600-700 ms gaps about every 1.7 s (roughly every 3000 steps); about 117 ms at speed 10. No rAF callback or long task exceeds 50 ms, --disable-gpu does not change it, and an idle page has none. A headless CDP trace came back empty. Suspect GC or Wasm memory growth tied to allocation (toHost every frame, batch arrays per step). Needs a headed Chrome performance profile (or --trace-gc) to find the cause, then a fix (for example reuse buffers, or publish host less often). Owns packages/web/src/state/trainSlice.ts (perf only). Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: Cause identified with a profile; at speed 50 no frame gap over 100 ms during 60 s of Run in headed Chrome on the SPEC example; liveArrays still flat.
close_reason: PR #49 merged. Cause: jax-js 0.1.27 Wasm backend did new WebAssembly.Instance per sync kernel dispatch (~44k/s at speed 50; 654k SyncInstantiate in 15 s trace); main-thread RunTasks of ~500 ms. Fix: pnpm patch caches program.kernelFunc (memory is created once per backend; worker path already caches). After: 0 gaps >100 ms in 60 s headed Chrome, throughput ~2x, liveArrays flat. Regression test engine/test/instances.test.ts (fails without patch: 6200 instances). Upstream jax-js issue not filed.

title: engine: dispose compiled models (free jit caches)
description: Each compile builds jitted predict/eval/step functions that are never disposed (no model disposal in the Engine interface). The PR #14 review measured about 0.19 MB per compiled model, and PR #18 found that jitted functions hold their captured constants. jax-js jit(...) returns a function with .dispose() that frees them. The web app recompiles on every edit and lr change. Add Engine.disposeModel(model), or dispose the previous model's jitted functions on recompile. This is a CONTRACTS s7 change: update s7 and the web engine.ts caller (tinker-27m.2) to dispose the old model when it compiles a new one. Owns packages/engine/src/index.ts, compile.ts, types.ts and the web engine.ts call site. Risk: high (use-after-dispose).
acceptance_criteria: Compiling and disposing 1000 models keeps liveArrays flat and RSS bounded. Using a disposed model throws one plain sentence. The web recompile path disposes the old model. CONTRACTS s7 updated.
notes: From PR #19 review: the plug point is web/src/state/trainSlice.ts resync, where 'rt.model = null' drops the old model without disposing it. Dispose it after disposeState(). restoreBest reuses the model, so it must not dispose. stopLoop() runs first, so there is no use-after-dispose there.
close_reason: PR #27 merged. Engine.disposeModel(model) frees predict/eval/step, trainMany and lossGrid jits (registered in Internals.disposables); every model-taking method throws 'This model was disposed.' before consuming args; double dispose no-op; Params/TrainStates stay valid arrays. Web resync disposes the old model and a compiled-but-unstarted one. Does NOT reduce RSS: jax-js 0.1.27 partialEvalFlat trace-stack leak (~0.32 MB/compile) - tinker-d7c. many.test.ts timeout 60 s.

title: Resample ×20 overlay with bias and variance
description: The bias and variance view (SPEC "Resampling overlay"). A "Resample × 20" button trains 20 copies of the current architecture, each on a fresh training set (same generator, new seeds) and a new initialisation, for the same number of steps as the current run, with engine.trainMany. 1-D: faint curves and their bold average over the fit plot, with the truth; 2-D: the mean surface only. Report bias² and variance averaged over the plotted input range (core/stats.ts biasVariance).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views" and the decisions section, CONTRACTS.md sections 6, 7.
Owns: packages/web/src/results/ResampleOverlay.tsx, packages/core/src/stats.ts (biasVariance + tests), the button in the results header.
If the current run has 0 steps, use 500 and say so on the overlay. Show a busy state; the page must not freeze longer than the spike's measured time (if over ~300 ms, file the Web Worker follow-up in the PR body).
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: biasVariance unit test: bias² + variance equals the mean squared error to the truth; a linear model on sine shows high bias and low variance, a 1-32-1 network at n = 20 the reverse (screenshots); overlay clears on any graph or data change.
notes: From PR #21 (trainMany) review: (1) trainMany is full batch only and needs the same n for every copy. Resampled sets from one generator have the same n, so that is fine, but if the main run uses mini-batches the overlay copies follow a different optimiser path: say the overlay trains full batch, or file mini-batch support. (2) Timing in Node: 20 copies x 1000 steps take about 0.72 s at n=40 and 5.8 s at n=500, over the 300 ms budget. Run it in a Web Worker or reduce steps/copies; n=500 on the main thread would freeze the page. (3) Duplicate seeds give identical copies. (4) Dropout copies drift up to about 6e-4 from single-copy runs over 100 steps (float32).
close_reason: PR #39 merged. core/stats.ts biasVariance (population variance; bias^2+variance = MSE to truth; skips non-finite copies). Resample x20 runs in a module Web Worker with its own engine (results/resampleWorker.ts + resampleRun.ts): fresh training set per copy (forked data seed, same n), new init, full batch for the current steps (500 if 0); curves on the fixed grid; mean + faint copies (1-D), mean surface (2-D); readout bias^2/variance/copies/diverged. resampleStore clears on graph/dataset change and terminates runs in flight. n=40 ~0.2-0.65 s, n=500 ~0.3-2 s, no main-thread long tasks; worker liveArrays 0 after runs.

title: engine: lossGrid for the loss-surface view
description: lossGrid(model, params, batch, axes, a, b) per CONTRACTS.md section 7: the training loss over a grid of two parameter values with every other parameter fixed, computed with vmap (or a loop if vmap is slow, measured).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views" (Loss surface), CONTRACTS.md section 7.
Owns: packages/engine/src/surface.ts (+ test).
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: On the two-parameter fixture, lossGrid at (w, b) equals evaluate with those values written; a 50×50 grid takes under 50 ms in Node (measured in the PR); no leak.
notes: From PR #18 review: any array constant captured in a jitted trace (for example an index array, or a constant created inside a random function) is never freed, because jitted functions are never disposed. Each compiled model then leaks it. Pass such arrays as jit arguments, or avoid them. Test by compiling 200 models in a loop with the probe and checking the live count stays flat.
close_reason: PR #20 merged. surface.ts lossGrid = jit(vmap) over grid points reusing evalFn (mean loss + penalty, dropout off); exact select overwrite of the two chosen entries; masks and grid values are jit args (no captured constants); output [a.length, b.length] row-major; chunked at points*rows <= 2^20 with padding. 50x50: 0.3 ms two_param, ~89 ms MLP n=500. Leak-probe blind spot (lazy all-equal arrays < 128 elems not counted) documented in probe.ts, spike.md s4, CONTRACTS s7.

design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views" (Resampling overlay), docs/spike.md (vmap timings), CONTRACTS.md section 7.

acceptance_criteria: Copy i of trainMany equals a single-model run with seed i on data i to 1e-5; k = 20 × 1000 steps on the 1-16-1 MLP completes within the spike's measured budget; no leak.
close_reason: PR #21 merged. many.ts trainMany = jit(vmap(stepFn)); per-copy seeds/init/data; same n and full batch only; returns ManyResult[] {params, diverged}; a diverged copy freezes at last finite state, others bit-identical. Also fixed compile.ts step finiteness check (jax-js folds x*0 to 0 even for NaN; now np.isfinite count) - test fails on old code. 20x1000 n=40 ~0.72 s Node, n=500 ~5.8 s: over the 300 ms overlay budget.

design:

title: engine: remaining losses and the weight penalty
description: Absolute error, Huber (delta), log loss (fused BCE with logits when the output is sigmoid), cross-entropy (fused log-softmax with softmax output), squared error on a sigmoid output, and the L1/L2 penalty over Linear weights only (CONTRACTS.md section 7).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Pieces" (the detail about combined numerically stable forms), CONTRACTS.md sections 4 and 7.
Owns: packages/engine/src/losses.ts, penalty.ts, and removing the matching skips in test/reference.test.ts.
Risk: high. Reviewer: log loss with logits of +/-50 must stay finite.
acceptance_criteria: The loss and penalty fixtures match; log loss and cross-entropy stay finite with logits of +/-50 (new test); evaluate includes the penalty and predict returns probabilities.
close_reason: PR #17 merged. losses.ts: absolute_error (np.abs), huber (nn.HuberLoss, a<delta quadratic), log_loss fused as logsumexp([z,0])-z*y (finite at logits +-1000), cross_entropy via logSoftmax+one-hot (k from z.shape). penalty.ts: lambda*sum w^2 / sum |w| over Linear W only; added in walk loss mode (evaluate+step, not predict), skipped at lambda 0. 8 fixtures at 1e-5 (worst 5.1e-6); penalty_l1_zero_weight skipped per owner. Independent numpy recompute agrees.

title: Shareable exercise links without rebuilding the app
description:
The instructor must be able to post a link to an exercise without rebuilding and redeploying the app. Today ?preset= accepts only a bundled preset name (web/src/main.tsx).

Why: exercises change week to week; bundling every one means a redeploy per change.

Open question (owner to choose):
(a) encode the model and settings in the URL (self-contained, works offline, but long URLs and no datasets bigger than the URL allows), or
(b) let ?preset= accept a URL to a preset file (short links, the file can be edited in place, but needs CORS and a network fetch, and conflicts with the 'no runtime requests' rule in tinker-ysl.4 unless user-initiated counts).
design:
Files likely involved: web/src/main.tsx, presets/index.ts, topbar/PresetMenu.tsx (loadBundled), topbar/FileMenu.tsx (loadParsed), core/src/file.ts (serialise/parse), topbar/csvSource.ts (existing URL fetch rules and error sentences to reuse).
Risk: normal. Security: a preset from a URL is data only; parseFile already validates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The chosen option loads a preset from a link in a fresh browser; failures give one plain sentence.
2. Locked pieces, disclosure and prompts survive the round trip.
3. pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass; CONTRACTS section 12 updated.
notes:
Owner decision 2026-11-22: option (a), encode the model and settings in the URL. Do after 6t7.15 (embedded CSV rows) merges.
From PR #105 review: serializeFile pretty-prints (2-space) with full-precision floats; 5000x10 csv is ~1.3 MB pretty / 0.9 MB compact, 5000x50 ~5 MB+. URL encoding needs compact JSON + compression and a deliberate rounding or size-cap decision (plain-sentence refusal when too big).
close_reason: PR #108: File > Copy link (file-copy-link) copies <origin><path>#x=1.<base64url(deflate-raw(compact saveText JSON))>; cap 32000 chars. startFromUrl in web/src/share/shareLink.ts decodes on start (link wins over ?preset=), caps fragment 200k chars and inflated size 16 MB, tolerates padding/%3D/+/. Failures one sentence; app starts normally.

title: Datasets saved with a preset or file (or referenced by URL)
description:
A loaded CSV should travel with a saved file or preset, or be referenced by URL, since exercises depend on specific data. Today a saved file records set: 'csv' but not the rows, and loading it in a session without that CSV is refused (CONTRACTS section 6).

Why: the instructor's own data for an exercise must reach every student exactly.
design:
Files likely involved: core/src/file.ts, data/csv.ts (registerCsv), common.ts (dataSchema), topbar/FileMenu.tsx, CsvDialog.tsx and csvSource.ts, CONTRACTS sections 6 and 12.
Risk: normal.
Open questions: embed rows (size limit; CSV_LIMITS is 5000 x 50) versus a URL reference (needs network and CORS); keep the build choices (target, inputs, kind) with it; how this interacts with the shareable-links bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Save a file after opening a CSV; open it in a fresh session; same rows, columns and kind, no refusal (test).
2. Presets can carry or reference a CSV the same way.
3. pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass; CONTRACTS updated.
notes: Owner decision 2026-11-22: embed rows in the saved file/preset (within CSV_LIMITS); no URL reference.
close_reason: PR #105: saved files/presets carry top-level csv field (built dataset: name, kind, features, target, classes, categories, raw x, y; stable key order) via core/data/csvEmbed.ts; validated with CSV_LIMITS and one-sentence errors. Undo/redo restore the matching CSV (WeakMap graph->csv in store.ts). Missing name -> 'your data'. serializeFile is pretty-printed full precision: 6t7.14 must compact/compress.

title: Per-preset success check with a visible tick
description:
A preset can name an optional condition, for example 'training loss below 0.3' or 'parameter b within 0.01 of 0.25', and the app shows a visible tick when it is met (and removes it when no longer met).

Why: students working alone know when they have done the exercise. SPEC lists 'automatic checks' under the later Lessons milestone; no bead existed for it.
design:
Files likely involved: core/src/file.ts (Preset field, validation), state/ (evaluate the condition from trainLoss/valLoss/host), a small indicator component, CONTRACTS section 12.
Risk: normal.
Open questions: the condition language (a few fixed kinds: loss below, parameter near, accuracy above; or a small expression); several checks per preset (one per instruction step); does a check latch once met?
acceptance_criteria:
1. A preset with a loss-below and a parameter-near check shows the tick exactly when met (tests for the evaluator).
2. Invalid checks are refused by parseFile with a plain sentence.
3. Browser check; pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass; CONTRACTS updated.
close_reason: PR #94: Preset.checks (core/src/checks.ts): lossBelow {value, split?, step?} (strict <, on liveLoss) and paramNear {node, tensor?, index?, value, tol, step?}; no latch; parseFile validates (incl. param/tensor/index existence when shapes are known; ids mapped for v1). Ticks: per step in InstructionsPanel li, shared tick in its header or a thin canvas row when the panel isn't shown. UI id success-check. No accuracyAbove (no accuracy computed yet).

title: Per-preset label overrides for readouts and controls
description:
Let a preset rename readouts and controls, for example 'lr' shown as 'Step size', the loss readout titled 'Average surprise', 'Run' shown as 'Keep stepping'. Labels not overridden stay as they are.

Why: the first class uses plain words before the technical names; later lessons drop the overrides and the standard names appear.

General mechanism, not a beginner-only special case (epic tinker-6t7). Use the same control ids as the disclosure bead.

(The request also asked to remove or gate the dev-only live-array readout in the training bar: already done. TrainingBar.tsx renders data-testid live-arrays only under import.meta.env.DEV, so production builds do not show it.)
design:
Files likely involved: core/src/file.ts (Preset field and validation), state/presetSlice.ts, trainbar/TrainingBar.tsx, results/LossReadout.tsx and panel headers, topbar/DataControls.tsx. SPEC principle 5: the text comes from the preset, the tool adds none.
Risk: low-normal.
Open questions: are labels plain text or allowed TeX (PromptLine uses TexText)? Length limits so the training bar still fits 1024 px.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A preset can override labels of the controls and readouts in the disclosure id list; others unchanged; aria-labels follow.
2. Training bar still fits at 1024x768 with long labels (truncate or wrap, state which).
3. CONTRACTS section 12 documents the field; pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass.
close_reason: PR #97: Preset.labels keyed by LABEL_IDS (subset of UI_IDS with visible text), plain text, max 40 chars; useUiLabel(id, fallback) in web/src/state/disclosure.ts; aria-labels follow; truncation with ellipsis in training bar, canvas header (capped widths) and data controls; travels with the preset in undo, Save writes it. Not checked at 1180x820/1920x1080.

title: Persistent instructions panel for multi-step exercise text
description:
A preset can supply multi-step exercise text shown in a panel that stays visible (and can be collapsed), as an alternative to the single dismissible prompt line (presets/PromptLine.tsx).

Why: each stage has several steps ('drag p until the score is largest', 'now press Step three times and fill the table'); a single dismissible line is not enough.
design:
Files likely involved: core/src/file.ts (Preset field), presets/ (new component beside PromptLine.tsx), App.tsx layout, state/presetSlice.ts. Region id joins the disclosure scheme. Text is from the preset only (SPEC principle 5).
Risk: low-normal.
Open questions: where it lives (above the canvas, in the results column, a side drawer) at 1024x768; numbered steps with optional ticks (ties to the success-check bead) or free text; TeX allowed like the prompt.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A preset with instructions shows them in a persistent panel; a preset without shows nothing new.
2. Collapsible; layout fits at section 10 viewports, light and dark, no page scroll.
3. pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass; CONTRACTS updated.
close_reason: PR #91: Preset.instructions?: string[] (TeX via TexText), presets/InstructionsPanel.tsx collapsible at top of canvas, list capped at 28vh; replaces the prompt line (prompt becomes the title); <li data-step> per step for 6t7.13 ticks; UI id 'instructions' (canvas group); Save writes it back. No bundled preset uses it yet.

title: Step log: a table row per Step with parameter values, prediction, slope and loss
description:
A small table that adds a row each time Step is pressed: step number, parameter value(s), prediction, slope (gradient) and loss. For small models only (hidden or truncated beyond a few parameters).

Why: stage 1. Gradient descent by hand: students compute the next step on paper and check it against the table.
design:
Files likely involved: new results panel in web/src/results/, state/trainSlice.ts (step; the gradient is not read back today), engine if gradients must be exposed (shared need with the tangent in the 1-D curve bead), panelLayout.ts. Panel id joins the disclosure scheme.
Risk: normal (high if engine changes).
Open questions:
- Does Run add rows too (capped), or only Step?
- Is the slope the gradient before the step (what the update used)? Proposed yes.
- Cleared on Reset; how many rows kept?
acceptance_criteria:
1. Each Step adds one row; the values match the parameters after the step and the gradient used (test against a hand calculation on the no-input preset).
2. Hidden or a plain sentence above a parameter limit.
3. Browser check at section 10 viewports, light and dark; pnpm test, typecheck, lint, build pass.
close_reason: PR #92: opt-in panel panel-step-log (results/StepLog.tsx); only Step adds rows (last 50); row = params and yhat after, slope (engine.lossSlope) and loss before; slopes shown only for plain sgd, full batch, no dropout; >4 scalar entries -> one sentence. Cleared on Reset, Restore best, load, structural change, hand edit; undo drops later rows. 1024x768 clipping fix (smaller font) not re-checked in a browser.

title: Resampling overlay (trainMany) does not range-check unfused cross-entropy probabilities
description: Follow-up from tinker-ddg review (PR #80). step() refuses an update when an unfused log_loss/cross_entropy pred leaves (0,1); trainMany uses the plain vmapped step. Unfused log_loss out of range gives NaN, so the copy is marked diverged (visible). Unfused cross_entropy with p[class] > 1 gives a finite negative loss, so the copy trains on a meaningless objective silently.
design: Risk: HIGH (engine). Pass the per-copy min/max ranges out of the vmapped step (as stepRangeFn does) and freeze a copy whose range leaves (0,1), like a diverged copy; report it as diverged (or a new flag) in ManyResult. Leak test.
acceptance_criteria: trainMany on a graph with unfused cross_entropy whose p[class] exceeds 1 freezes that copy and flags it; other copies bit-identical; leak test passes.
close_reason: PR #81: trainMany vmaps stepRangeFn for models with unfused prob losses; copies whose pred leaves (0,1) freeze and report diverged. Reviewer: no issues; untested P>1 / mixed fused+unfused; resample message 'Every copy diverged' slightly off for range cause (left as is).

title: web: 2-D fit plot polish (smooth truth boundary, greyscale-distinct ramp, point contrast)
description: From PR #32 review: (1) the classification truth boundary is contoured from a binary 0/1 field on the 64 grid, so the circle's boundary is jagged; contour a smooth signed field instead. (2) --div-neg/--div-pos endpoints have nearly equal lightness (especially in dark), so a greyscale print loses the class distinction; adjust the tokens so lightness differs too. (3) regression points use the surface ramp and nearly vanish on same-coloured regions (saddle); add a contrasting outline or halo. Owns results/FitPlot2D.tsx, plot/surface.ts, theme.css --div-*/--seq-* tokens. Risk: low (UI: screenshots).
acceptance_criteria: Circle truth boundary visibly smooth; ramp endpoints differ by >= 25 in CIE L* in light and dark; regression points visible on every region of plane/bowl/saddle; screenshots light and dark.
notes: From PR #35: the Output piece's link name under yhat is still tiny at fit scale on long graphs; apply legibleAt(scale) from canvas/pure.ts to it too.
close_reason: PR #41 merged. Smooth truth boundary via core truthMargin(set, xRaw) signed field (circle, xor, blobs, moons) contoured at 0; --div-neg/--div-pos lightness gap 33.9 (light) / 28.5 (dark) L*, tested from theme.css; --point-halo outline on regression points; Output link name hidden below 8 px via legibleAt.

title: web: 'controlled to uncontrolled input' warning after loadGraph
description: Seen in PR #28 and PR #31: React logs 'A component is changing a controlled input to be uncontrolled' after store.loadGraph (and maybe a file/preset load). A field likely reads an optional graph setting (for example huber delta, penalty lambda, seed, or a data field) that becomes undefined after the load.
